transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Hayes: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan on the AE side at Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Lena Park: Lena here, hi.
[00:08] Marcus Wu: Marcus.
[00:09] Riley Gomez: Riley.
[00:10] Avery Kim: Avery.
[00:12] Priya Natarajan: Priya from Redwood, hi all.
[00:15] Jordan Hayes: Cool, goal for the call — figure out how quickly SparkBridge can get first token on Redwood and the path from PLG free credits to a small POC, plus any blockers like VPC or compliance.
[00:26] Marcus Wu: Sounds good. We're evaluating both hosted and the private route but we want to see how fast our devs can hit an endpoint. We like low friction — curl, node sdk, etc.
[00:35] Jordan Hayes: Absolutely. Our typical PLG flow is: sign up, get free credits that show in the console, then run a quickstart curl or SDK that gets you a token in minutes. Time-to-first-token we usually see is sub-10 minutes if you follow the quickstart.
[00:47] Avery Kim: Sub-10 is ideal. On the security side, we'll need SOC2 docs, also KMS for keying, and we may need a private deployment later.
[00:57] Priya Natarajan: We can cover that. Hosted works for most teams; Dedicated or Private comes in when you need fixed capacity or strict network isolation. For the POC, hosted plus VPC egress controls usually suffices.
[01:12] Riley Gomez: Quick question — credits expire? And can we limit who uses credits across our org?
[01:18] Jordan Hayes: Credits typically have a 90-day window for the PLG package, and you can scope them to an account in the console. We'll include the exact expiry in the credit email.
[01:26] Marcus Wu: Great. For benchmarking we care about latency at 1k concurrent requests and cost per 1M tokens.
[01:33] Priya Natarajan: For hosted we'll run a baseline: token latency p50/p95 on your prompt set. For concurrent throughput we'll propose a short stress test using our load harness — that's what we'll schedule next.
[01:44] Jordan Hayes: On-boarding: the quickstart has 3 steps: create account, accept credits, run curl or SDK to get first token. We also have templates (Node/Python) that integrate fast.
[01:55] Lena Park: Any gotchas for kafka-backed APIs or long context windows? We have a bunch of conversational context; sequence lengths can spike.
[02:03] Priya Natarajan: We logged that — longer contexts change kernel selection and batching. We can recommend quantization and chunking strategies if cost becomes an issue. Also our runtime supports longer KV cache optimization, but it's something to profile.
[02:18] Marcus Wu: If we wanted Dedicated later, is there a migration path without rewriting code?
[02:23] Jordan Hayes: Yes, same API. You can pin model versions and switch routing policies. The SDK and endpoints stay consistent — mostly config change on the backend.
[02:33] Riley Gomez: Firewalls — we run strict egress policies. Does Redwood support VPC peering or private link?
[02:40] Priya Natarajan: For Private we can do VPC peering and on-prem packages. For Hosted we support customer-managed egress + IP allowlists and outbound TLS — we also offer private-connect for enterprise customers. We'll share architecture diagrams.
[02:55] Avery Kim: Can you run a small pre-configured POC — say 50k tokens and a couple of endpoints — to test integration?
[03:02] Jordan Hayes: Yes, that's the typical first step after credits. We'll allocate a sandbox account and top it with credits so your engineers can push requests.
[03:12] Marcus Wu: For the quickstart, are there rate limits by default? Our app spikes sometimes.
[03:17] Jordan Hayes: Default rate limits are conservative for PLG accounts; we can temporarily raise them for the benchmark. For production you can request higher quotas or reserve Dedicated capacity.
[03:25] Lena Park: Do you provide example billing estimates? We need to compare unit economics against our current provider.
[03:31] Priya Natarajan: We have a cost model worksheet — we'll send a tailored estimate based on your prompt lengths and expected QPS. That's part of the benchmark deliverable.
[03:41] Marcus Wu: Competitors — you mentioned Replicate and Anthropic earlier, anything we should watch for?
[03:46] Jordan Hayes: Some providers make different tradeoffs — Anthropic on instruction tuning, OpenAI on dev experience, Replicate on easy self-hosting. Redwood focuses on production inference economics and predictable latency across hosted/dedicated/private.
[03:58] Riley Gomez: Any SDK quirks we should know — like streaming vs chunked streaming?
[04:03] Priya Natarajan: We support streaming in SDKs (Node, Python, Go). For high-concurrency workloads streaming helps reduce perceived latency but increases connection counts — we'll cover that in the runbook.
[04:17] Jordan Hayes: Ok, let's walk through the quickstart live — I'll paste the curl snippet in chat and we can try a token exchange.
[04:23] Jordan Hayes: (shares link) curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/token -H 'Authorization: Bearer <api_key>' -d '{"model":"redwood-1.2","input":"Hello"}' — this is pseudo, exact quickstart will be in the doc.
[04:38] Marcus Wu: Awesome, our dev is going to try that after the call.
[04:40] Lena Park: Any internal SSO support? We use Okta.
[04:43] Jordan Hayes: Yes, SAML/Okta for enterprise console. For PLG self-serve it's email/SSO link; enterprise accounts get SSO onboarding.
[04:51] Avery Kim: Re: data retention — do you store prompts by default? We need clarity for GDPR.
[04:56] Priya Natarajan: We can configure retention policies. For enterprise we offer short retention and configurable deletion hooks. We'll send the data handling policy doc.
[05:06] Riley Gomez: If we toggle to Private later, is the data plane isolated?
[05:10] Priya Natarajan: Yes — Private deploys have customer-managed control plane options and full network isolation, and you can plug in your KMS/HSM.
[05:19] Jordan Hayes: Ok timeline — we'll send credits today/tomorrow, you'll spin up quickstart, then schedule a 60-min benchmark with Priya & Marcus. Any constraints on next week?
[05:28] Marcus Wu: Next Wed or Thu works for us.
[05:31] Jordan Hayes: Perfect. Anything else?
[05:33] Lena Park: No, that's it from my side. Thanks.
[05:35] Jordan Hayes: Great, recap in chat and action items. Thanks all.
[05:40] (call ends)
